title: Resumable delta + attachment-aware metering ledger
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Problem: We observe two classes of billing discrepancies in resumed streaming flows: (1) delta-encoded patch replays where the client sends only diffs after a reconnect and token counts diverge from original full-state tokenization, and (2) resumed flows containing binary attachments (images/audio) whose client-side pre-tokenization length heuristics differ from server-side canonical tokenization, producing orphaned or duplicate charges. Goal: introduce a compact, resumable ledger format and reconciliation protocol that is attachment-aware and supports delta patches without requiring clients to always re-send full prefixes. Scope: server-side ledger markers, patch canonicalization rules, idempotency checksums for patches, attachment fingerprinting and token-length heuristics alignment, reconciliation job + retroactive corrections, dashboarding, and rollout behind a feature flag. Key constraints: keep per-request latency impact minimal (<=1ms median added), avoid storing full upstream payloads for more than 48 hours for cost/privacy, maintain auditability for chargebacks, be compatible with existing quota enforcement and rate limits, and preserve backward compatibility for older clients. Proposed approach: - Introduce PatchLedger entries: compact events that record (patch_id, base_snapshot_checksum, patch_checksum, applied_range, token_delta_estimate, attachment_fingerprints). PatchLedger entries are append-only and anchored to session snapshots. - Canonicalization: on receipt of a patch, compute a canonicalized representation used for token counting (normalize unicode, strip protocol wrappers, expand macro tokens that affect tokenizer length). For attachments, compute a stable fingerprint (SHA256 of transform pipeline result) and a deterministic token-length estimate mapping per attachment mime/type. - Idempotency: require clients to include client_patch_id; server will dedupe using (session_id, client_patch_id) and compare checksums; mismatches trigger a short reconciliation path. - Reconciliation: nightly job that replays ledger markers against the canonical tokenizer with deterministic random seeds to produce final per-session token tallies and emits retroactive corrections for sessions where provisional credits differ >1 token or >0.5% cost threshold. - Charging model: provisional credits applied on append; final credits finalized after reconciliation window (default 24h). For high-value customers we will expose an opt-in ImmediateFinalization mode that pays the cost of running real-time reconciliation. - Metrics & Alerts: new perf counters (ledger_write_latency_ms, patch_reconciliation_skew_tokens, attachment_fingerprint_mismatch_rate), SLA alert on skew_tokens > 100 per hour for production. - Migration & compatibility: clients without client_patch_id will fall back to legacy full-resend path; servers will attempt heuristic prefix-reconciliation but mark these sessions for higher scrutiny. Rollout: start with internal traffic, then opt-in beta customers, then gradual 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollout with toggles per-tenant. Open questions: - How to set deterministic token-length mapping for compressed audio attachments? - Storage TTL for patch payloads needed to support auditors/customers for chargebacks? - Edge behavior for simultaneous parallel patches (concurrent client windows). Implementation plan: 1) Design and proto for PatchLedger (jackpot: small binary proto) + tests (unit + e2e sandbox). 2) Implement canonicalizer module shared by billing and runtime token counter. 3) Server-side ledger write path + quick dedupe in request path. 4) Reconciler job with test harness and sample historical backfill tool. 5) Dashboards and billing export schema changes. 6) Client SDK guidance + patch id requirement. Acceptance criteria: deterministic reconciler output on synthetic corpus, end-to-end integration test demonstrating no more than 1 in 10k sessions with >2 token final/provisional delta, and monitoring dashboards show reconciliation skew trending to zero after rollouts.
comments: 2026-01-16 — Jordan Lee: Initial spike finished. Verified that client_patch_id is feasible to require in new SDKs. Small perf spike on canonicalizer (p95 +0.6ms) in prototype; need micro-optimizations.

2026-01-21 — Aisha Patel: Design review with PM and runtime. Decided to keep provisional credits model; PM wants a 24h default window and opt-in immediate finalization for enterprise. Linked design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/PatchLedger+Design

2026-01-28 — EngInfra: PoC for attachment fingerprinting completed. For PNGs we'll normalize by stripping metadata and running a quick rescale to a canonical DPI before hashing. Audio pipeline raises more questions — lossy formats will use duration+codec+approx-frame-count heuristic as fallback.

2026-02-03 — QA: Found race when two near-simultaneous patches arrive with overlapping applied_range; introduced per-session sequence number check and fallback merge semantics. Added unit test case 'overlap-merge-should-stabilize'.

2026-02-10 — Aisha Patel: Created draft PR for ledger proto + canonicalizer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821 — needs perf review. Also added preliminary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/patchledger/patch-reconciliation

2026-02-18 — Security: Asked for threat modelling document for attachment fingerprinting pipeline and storage TTL. Reply: will keep payloads encrypted at rest, TTL 48h default and support extended retention for audits via enterprise contract.

2026-02-20 — Jordan Lee: Reconciler harness passed deterministic corpus tests (1M synthetic sessions). Next: run staging backfill against 7 days of traffic and evaluate retroactive correction volume before canary.
